note: Two words that are NOT spatial shapes but are still legitimate targets, because a trigger already knows who the other party was. COMBAT-DESIGN's own hook notes establish the concept: onMiss fires 'on the ATTACKER', onDodge 'on the DEFENDER'. A shape answers 'which hexes'; a referent answers 'the one this event was already about', and no shape can say that. Declared here as data so that audit R27 can accept them without anyone inventing a third one in code. Ruled 2026-08-22.

referents.name: the attacker
referents.means: whoever caused the damage that fired this trigger
referents.why: Hitting back at whoever hit you is what onTakingDamage is FOR. Ban 19 forbids reading the attacker's TAGS OR POSITION — conditioning on who they are — not striking them. Thorns N is the passive form of the same idea; this is the triggered form.

referents.name: the unit this hit
referents.means: the target of the attack this effect is riding on
referents.why: A rider on an attack acts on what the attack acted on. The source called this 'attacked'.

referents.name: the unit this missed
referents.means: the target of the attack this effect is riding on, when that attack missed
referents.why: The exact mirror of "the unit this hit", and needed for the same reason: a rider on an attack acts on what the attack was aimed at. Declared 2026-09-02 for the Dark Sniper’s Long Shot, whose whole design is that the miss still costs you. A spatial shape cannot say it, and on an enemy a raw source string reads backwards.
